title: No Change of Times Shall Ever Shock
description: No Change of Times Shall Ever Shock in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Nahum Tate and Nicholas Brady wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 624 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Confidence in the Divine Care”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: No change of times shall ev-er shock My firm af-fec-tion, Lord, to thee; For thou hast al-ways been a rock, A for-tress and de-fence to me.

lines: No change of times shall ever shock
My firm affection, Lord, to thee;
For thou hast always been a rock,
A fortress and defence to me.
Thou my Deliverer art, my God;
My trust is in thy mighty power;
Thou art my shield from foes abroad,
At home my safeguard and my tower.
To heaven I made my mournful prayer,
To God addressed my humble moan,
And heard me from his lofty throne.
Who, then, deserves to be adored,
But God, on whom my hopes depend?
Or who, except the mighty Lord,

licence: Public domain: Nahum Tate died in 1715; Nicholas Brady died in 1726.
credits: Words by Nahum Tate (1652–1715) and Nicholas Brady (1659–1726), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
